What happens to your super when you die? (Australia)

By the Afterkeep research team · Reviewed on 19 Oct 2026

Your super doesn't automatically form part of your estate. In most cases the fund pays your balance, plus any insurance held in super, as a death benefit to your nominated beneficiary. A valid binding nomination means the fund must follow your choice; without one, the trustee decides. Check your nomination in your fund's app or website.

Key facts

  • Super isn't automatically part of your estate
  • Lapsing binding nominations expire after 3 years
  • Non-dependants can only receive a lump sum
  • The death benefit can include insurance held in super

What are the steps?

  1. Log in to each super fund (website or app) and check whether you have a nomination, what type it is and whether it expires.
  2. Ask your fund which nomination types it offers. Not every fund offers every type.
  3. Choose eligible people: a spouse or partner, children of any age, someone in an interdependency relationship with you, someone financially dependent on you, or your legal personal representative (your estate).
  4. Want someone who isn't a dependant to benefit? The ATO suggests asking your fund about a binding nomination to your legal personal representative, so the money is distributed under your will. Keep your will up to date.
  5. Follow the form's signing and witnessing instructions exactly. Moneysmart warns that mistakes can make a nomination invalid.
  6. If it's a lapsing binding nomination, set a reminder. These expire after 3 years unless you renew them.
  7. List each fund, member number and any insurance in your estate inventory. Leave passwords out.
  8. After a death: the beneficiary or executor contacts each fund to report the death and ask about releasing the super, and checks whether the person had ATO-held super.

Frequently asked questions

Does super go through my will?

Not automatically. Moneysmart says super doesn't automatically form part of your estate. It's distributed under your will only if it's paid to your legal personal representative (your estate).

What is a binding death benefit nomination?

An instruction your fund must follow to pay your super to the eligible people you name. Lapsing ones must be renewed every 3 years; non-lapsing ones don't expire. Not every fund offers them.

What happens if I don't nominate anyone?

The ATO says the fund trustee may use its discretion to decide which dependants receive it, or pay it to your legal personal representative to be distributed under your will.

Who can I nominate for my super?

Your spouse or partner, your children of any age, someone in an interdependency relationship with you, anyone financially dependent on you, or your legal personal representative.

Can a non-dependant receive super as an income stream?

No. The ATO says a death benefit paid to someone who isn't a dependant must be paid as a lump sum.

How do I find a deceased person's super?

Contact the funds you know about and check whether the person had ATO-held super. The ATO can give super fund details to the authorised legal personal representative.
